commons.title: Limbu Alphabet Chart (ᤕᤠᤰᤌᤢᤱ ᤐᤠᤴ).png
commons.description: Limbu Alphabet Chart (ᤕᤠᤰᤌᤢᤱ ᤐᤠᤴ) in Noto Sans font (Regular)This chart is divided into:25 basic consonants (ᤁᤢᤎᤰ ᤙᤰᤛᤠ) - ᤁ ᤂ ᤃ ᤅ ᤆ ᤇ ᤈ ᤏ ᤋ ᤌ ᤍ ᤎ ᤐ ᤑ ᤒ ᤓ ᤔ ᤕ ᤖ ᤗ ᤘ ᤙ ᤛ ᤜ ᤄ, and one vowel carrier ᤀ,9 Vowel diacritics (ᤁᤢᤒᤢᤱ ᤙᤰᤛᤠ) with vowel carrier "ᤀ" -  ᤀᤠ ᤀᤡ ᤀᤢ ᤀᤣ ᤀᤤ ᤀᤥ ᤀᤦ ᤀᤧ ᤀᤨ,8 Half letters (ᤁᤧᤍᤢᤶᤒᤠ ᤙᤰᤛᤠ or ᤆᤢᤰ ᤙᤰᤛᤠ) with base letter "ᤁ" - ᤁᤰ ᤁᤱ ᤁᤴ ᤁᤳ ᤁᤵ ᤁᤶ ᤁᤷ ᤁᤸ,3 Subjoined glides (ᤀᤣᤁ᤻ᤋᤢᤶ ᤙᤰᤛᤠ) -  ᤩ    ᤪ    ᤫ,3 special diacritics (ᤁᤢᤛᤣᤁ᤻ ᤙᤰᤛᤠ) with vowel carrier "ᤀ" - ᤀ᤺ (ᤁᤣᤶᤓᤪᤧᤱ), ᤀ᤹ (ᤔᤢᤰᤑᤪᤧᤱ), ᤀ᤻ (ᤛᤀᤡ).10 Limbu specific numerals (ᤂᤠᤏᤡᤋ᤻) - ᥆ ᥇ ᥈ ᥉ ᥊ ᥋ ᥌ ᥍ ᥎ ᥏,and 3 punctuation marks - ॥ ᥄ ᥅Letters ᤉ ᤊ ᤚ ᤝ ᤞ ᥀ were removed from Modern Limbu and thus are not depicted.
commons.editorial_reason: Alphabet chart is a digital graphic, not a visible cultural artifact or practice.

commons.title: "Silam-Sakma" a symbol identifying the Limboo tribe.jpg
commons.description: A modern Limboo house in "Mathlo gaon" a village in Panchthar district in Eastern Nepal. This symbol is generally conspicuous only at a Limboo house as an indication of Limboo resident. Since houses nowadays are so visually diverse that a particular house has stopped representing itself for a distinct community. Limboo people have started to display this symbol in the house to express their identity.
commons.editorial_reason: Description specifically attributes the house symbol and architecture to Limboo identity.

commons.title: Limboo house in Hee- kengbari village in West Sikkim, Sikkim, India.jpg
commons.description:
Vernacular house of the Limboo( Limbu, Yakthung, Subba) tribes of Sikkim, North-East of India.  It is similar to the Limbu house in Eastern Nepal. 
This house exists in Hee- kengbari village in West Sikkim, Sikkim. Its atleast 75-80 years old.

 The house of Limboos is a symbolic representation of Yuma- a goddess of the Limboo community.
commons.editorial_reason: Description explicitly attributes the vernacular house to the Limboo/Limbu community.

commons.title: Sikuwa(in Nepali term) .jpg
commons.description:
"Sikuwa" is a semi-open space which is the most active space in the entire house. This semi-private is generally allocated for the guests to sit and also utilised for storage of objects like "janto" or a stone grinder and other traditional household appliances.
This view is a part of a house in Bagale village in Panchthar district in East Nepal
commons.editorial_reason: Shows a generic house space in Nepal; the description does not specifically attribute it to Limbu culture.

commons.title: "Muring-Sitlam" or the main pillar.jpg
commons.description: This main holy pillar is seen generally in every Limboo house and is considered as holy due to the representation of it as the shrine to Yuma goddess which is devoted by the Limboo tribal people. The belief is sustained due to an old tribal myth.
commons.editorial_reason: Description specifically identifies the visible pillar as a holy feature of Limboo houses tied to Yuma worship.
